newsitem.title: USA: U.S. July spot natgas firms in West due to heat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. July spot natgas firms in West due to heat.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were talked mostly higher Monday as heat still smothered the South and Northeast, market sources said.
Trading was light though as nomination deadlines for July 1 were complete and the upcoming Independence Day holiday discouraged some buyers from entering the market.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices were notionally quoted steady at $2.15-2.17 per mmBtu at the Henry Hub, still off about 15 cents from June indices.
Permian basin prices gained about four cents to the low-$2 area as thermometers topped 100 degrees F in western Texas.
Similarly at the southern California border prices rose two cents to about $2.15-2.18.
Helping to boost the market was news that the 1,070 megawatt San Onofre 2 nuclear unit had tripped off line. The unit is expected to return to service around July 15.
Meanwhile, San Juan prices jumped to about $2 amid heat and loss of nuclear power in California, traders said.
In the East, swing prices at the New York city-gate were quoted a bit higher at $2.46-2.47.
Forecasts are calling for continued warmer-than-normal weather in the region through Thursday, with highs expected in the mid-to-high 80s F.
In the Midwest, swing prices were also quoted a few cents higher at $2.02-2.04.
"It was busier than I expected. Normally, it's so quiet on the last day, but there were definitely some buyers out there that needed some gas," one Midwest trader said.
Chicago city-gate for next month was talked equally firmer around $2.25.
